question: Does the proposed walking-policy reset preserve explicit failure and clear actual recurrent state before later inference?
scope: Local CPU source review and controlled runtime regression. The author owns the original report and integration. No hardware, locomotion-quality, whole-PR approval, owner effort or independent reuse claim.
fixture: Run the full g1_teleop.run_teleop function with real MuJoCo scene loading and controlled viewer, keyboard, time and mj_step. Stateful policy doubles distinguish successful, failed, unsupported and partially available reset contracts. Separately load the shipped TorchScript model on CPU and compare recurrence after reset to a fresh load on the same synthetic observation.

expected.initial_reset_failure: Error escapes; zero physics steps and policy calls after failure.
expected.manual_reset_failure: Error escapes before the next physics step or inference; keyboard/viewer clean up.
expected.fall_reset_failure: Error escapes after triggering step; zero later physics steps or inference; cleanup.
expected.viewer_reset: Callback only schedules input; reset executes in control thread before another step. A reset error must reach run_teleop, not remain on viewer callback thread.
expected.normal_reset: Fresh, manual and fall resets clear hidden and cell state. Native successful reset and force controls keep passing.
expected.unsupported: No reset API or incomplete/non-tensor fallback must raise rather than silently claim reset.
expected.shipped_policy: After a nonempty synthetic prefix and exported reset_memory, hidden/cell are zero and first output matches separately freshly loaded policy exactly.

controls: Preserve a failure-injection observation separately from assertion pass counts. Retain unchanged upstream and proposed patch runs. No changing acceptance after seeing results.
costs: Record setup, source acquisition, test duration and adaptations. No claim these total owner time or measure savings.
stop: If the head changes or an existing fix covers the finding, reassess before sending. Limit contribution to concrete reset behavior; do not take over the broad integration.
